licenses.excludes: AP·로이터·AFP 같은 통신사의 기사·사진·영상은 쓰지 않는다

expressions.note_ko: 사이에 목적어를 넣을 수 있다: give the papers out = give out the papers. 대명사는 꼭 사이에: give them out

examples.en: The teacher gave out the test papers.
They gave out free water at the race.

expressions.note_ko: 새 일, 프로젝트, 책임처럼 부담이 있는 것을 기꺼이 맡을 때. 직장에서 자주 쓴다

examples.en: I can take on one more project this month.
examples.ko: 이번 달에 프로젝트 하나 더 맡을 수 있어요.

examples.en: She took on the role of team leader.

expressions.note_ko: 시험·면접·발표 직전에 친구나 동료에게. 대답은 Good luck! 또는 You've got this!

examples.en: My interview is in ten minutes. Wish me luck!
I'm going to ask for a raise. Wish me luck.
examples.ko: 월급 올려 달라고 말해 보려고요. 행운을 빌어 줘요.

expressions.note_ko: at 뒤에는 명사나 ~ing. 못하면 be bad at ~ing, 보통이면 be OK at

examples.en: He's good at fixing computers.
I'm not good at remembering names.

expressions.note_ko: to 뒤에 장소가 오면 '그곳으로 돌아가다', ~ing가 오면 '그 일을 다시 하다'

examples.en: After lunch, let's go back to work.
She went back to studying after the break.

expressions.note_ko: 사람·회사가 함께 일할 때. 회사끼리 협업할 때도 쓴다: Two companies teamed up

examples.en: I teamed up with Mina for the presentation.
Two cafés teamed up to hold a music night.
examples.ko: 카페 두 곳이 손잡고 음악의 밤을 열었어요.

expressions.note_ko: 제안을 들었을 때 반응. great 자리에 good, fun, even better, interesting을 바꿔 넣는다

examples.en: Dinner at seven? That sounds great.
A trip to Busan? That sounds fun!

expressions.note_ko: 상대 말이 애매할 때 정중하게 되묻기. 말투가 세면 따지는 느낌이 날 수 있다
similar: What do you mean by that?

examples.en: What do you mean by 'soon'?
Sorry, what do you mean?

expressions.note_ko: 자기소개·면접에서 자주 쓴다. 반대는 not a people person

examples.en: I'm a people person, so I like working in sales.
examples.ko: 저는 사람을 좋아해서 영업 일이 좋아요.

examples.en: He's not really a people person.
examples.ko: 그는 사람들과 잘 어울리는 편은 아니에요.

expressions.note_ko: 카페·도서관에서 빈 의자나 콘센트를 쓰기 전에. 앞에 Excuse me를 붙이면 더 정중하다

examples.en: Excuse me, are you using this outlet?
Is anyone using this table?

expressions.note_ko: for 뒤에 ~ing나 명사. Thanks for coming / Thanks for your help

examples.en: Thanks for waiting.
Thanks for showing me around the city.

expressions.note_ko: busy 뒤에 to를 쓰지 않는다: busy to look (X)

examples.en: I'm busy preparing for the meeting.
She was busy packing for her trip.

expressions.note_ko: 사이에 목적어를 넣을 수 있다: tear the letter up. want ad는 '구인 광고'

examples.en: He tore up the old receipts.
Don't tear it up. We need it.

expressions.note_ko: 대명사는 꼭 사이에: throw it away (throw away it은 X)

examples.en: Please throw away your cup after the movie.
I threw the old shoes away.

expressions.note_ko: 일·과제·문제를 붙잡고 있을 때. 회사에서 What are you working on?(무슨 일 하고 있어요?)

examples.en: I'm working on a new report.
We're working on the problem.

expressions.note_ko: Forget about it.은 '신경 쓰지 마'라는 위로·사양의 말로도 쓴다

examples.en: Forget about work this weekend.
I forgot about the meeting!

expressions.note_ko: 상대가 할 말이 있다고 할 때 '계속해 보라'는 반응. 귀가 작은 토끼의 말버릇!

examples.en: You have an idea? I'm listening.
OK, I'm listening. What happened?

expressions.note_ko: I thought of you.는 '네 생각이 났어'. think about은 '곰곰이 생각하다'

examples.en: I saw this cake and thought of you.
examples.ko: 이 케이크를 보고 네 생각이 났어.

examples.en: Can you think of a better name?
examples.ko: 더 좋은 이름 떠오르는 거 있어요?

expressions.match: I don't have time right now
expressions.text: I don't have time right now.
expressions.note_ko: 앞에 Sorry를 붙이면 부드럽다. 나중에 하자면 Can we talk later?
similar: I'm a bit busy right now.

examples.en: Sorry, I don't have time right now. Can we talk later?
examples.ko: 미안해요, 지금은 시간이 없어요. 나중에 얘기할까요?

examples.en: I don't have time right now, but I'll call you tonight.
examples.ko: 지금은 시간이 없지만 오늘 밤에 전화할게요.

expressions.note_ko: 면접·첫 만남 전에 긴장한 사람에게 하는 격려

examples.en: Don't worry about the date. Just be yourself.
examples.ko: 소개팅 걱정 마. 그냥 너답게 해.

examples.en: In the interview, just be yourself.

expressions.note_ko: 물건을 건넬 때. 여러 개면 Here are ~. 짧게 Here you go.

examples.en: Here's my phone number.
Here are your tickets.

expressions.note_ko: Thanks for coming in.은 면접·상담에 와 준 사람에게 하는 인사. Come in!은 '들어오세요'

examples.en: Can you come in at nine tomorrow?
examples.ko: 내일 아홉 시에 와 줄 수 있어요?

examples.en: Come in, the door is open.

expressions.note_ko: 모르던 사실을 조사하거나 물어서 알게 될 때. find는 '찾다', find out은 '알아내다'

examples.en: Let me find out if the store is open.
I found out that the flight was delayed.

expressions.note_ko: To be honest, ~(솔직히 말하면)로 문장을 시작하는 말버릇도 자주 쓴다

examples.en: To be honest, I didn't like the movie.
Please be honest with me.

expressions.note_ko: 면접 단골 질문: What are you most proud of?(가장 자랑스러운 일은?)

examples.en: I'm proud of my team.
She's proud of finishing the marathon.

expressions.note_ko: 집중하려고 혼자 들어앉을 때. 실수로 갇혔을 때는 lock oneself out(밖에 잠겨 못 들어가다)과 헷갈리지 않기

examples.en: I locked myself in my room to study.
He locked himself in the studio for a week.

expressions.note_ko: the whole time과 같다. 시작부터 끝까지 계속

examples.en: It rained the entire time we were in London.
I was nervous the entire time.

expressions.note_ko: 말투에 따라 '이제 알겠다'(중립)도, '더 듣기 싫다'(차가움)도 된다

examples.en: Thank you, I've heard enough. You're hired.
Stop. I've heard enough excuses.

expressions.meaning_ko: 사람을 잘 다룬다 / 사람 대하는 게 서툴다
expressions.note_ko: good with + 대상: good with kids(아이들을 잘 본다), good with numbers(숫자에 강하다)

examples.en: She's really good with kids.
I'm not good with numbers.

expressions.note_ko: 면접 결과를 말할 때. 떨어지면 I didn't get the job.

examples.en: Guess what? I got the job!
He didn't get the job, but he's OK.

expressions.note_ko: 예상이 맞았을 때. 좋은 일에도 나쁜 일에도 쓴다

examples.en: You passed? I knew it!
It's raining. I knew it.

expressions.note_ko: 말할 때는 go and celebrate에서 and를 빼고 go celebrate처럼 말하는 경우가 많다

examples.en: Let's go eat something.
Let's go see a movie tonight.

sentences.speaker: Ms. Weaver

contents.title: Words to Travel With, Part 2: Airports

sentences.en: Ask one hundred people whether they love to travel and most of them will probably say yes.
sentences.ko: 100명에게 여행을 좋아하느냐고 물으면 아마 대부분 그렇다고 할 거예요.

sentences.en: Discovering a new place can be fun and exciting.
sentences.ko: 새로운 곳을 발견하는 건 재미있고 신나는 일이죠.

sentences.en: But getting to that place is often a lot less enjoyable.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그곳까지 가는 길은 그만큼 즐겁지 않을 때가 많아요.

sentences.en: Flying is a popular travel method.
But airports can be frustrating places.
sentences.ko: 그런데 공항은 답답한 곳일 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Having to speak a foreign language in an airport can add to the frustration.
sentences.ko: 공항에서 외국어로 말해야 하면 답답함이 더 커지기도 하고요.

sentences.en: Today, we will share some English phrases that can help you survive any airport experience!
sentences.ko: 오늘은 어떤 공항에서든 버틸 수 있게 도와줄 영어 표현을 나눠 볼게요!

sentences.en: Let’s begin with check-in.
At an airport, check-in is where you go to let the airline know that you have arrived.
sentences.ko: 공항에서 체크인은 항공사에 도착했다고 알리러 가는 곳이에요.

sentences.en: At check-in, you can also get your boarding pass.
sentences.ko: 체크인할 때 탑승권도 받을 수 있어요.

sentences.en: The document has your flight information on it.
It is proof that you purchased the flight.
You cannot get on the plane without one.
sentences.ko: 탑승권이 없으면 비행기를 탈 수 없어요.

sentences.en: Many airports offer two ways to check in: through a machine or with an airline employee.
sentences.ko: 많은 공항에서 체크인하는 방법이 두 가지예요. 기계로 하거나 항공사 직원에게 하는 거죠.

sentences.en: Here is what you’ll be asked if you get your boarding pass from the employee:
sentences.ko: 직원에게 탑승권을 받을 때 듣게 될 말은 이거예요.

sentences.en: Hello!
May I see your ID?
Your ID is your identification, such as a passport or driving document.
You can answer, “Sure” or “Here you go” and give the person the document.
sentences.ko: "Sure"나 "Here you go"라고 대답하고 서류를 건네면 돼요.

sentences.en: If you use the machine, you can enter the ticket or reservation number you received when you purchased the flight.
sentences.ko: 기계를 쓰면 항공권을 살 때 받은 티켓 번호나 예약 번호를 입력하면 돼요.

sentences.en: At the check-in area, you can also check your bags.
sentences.ko: 체크인하는 곳에서 짐도 부칠 수 있어요.

sentences.en: This means giving your bags, also called luggage, to an airline employee to be stored during the flight.
sentences.ko: 가방, 다른 말로 짐을 항공사 직원에게 맡겨서 비행하는 동안 보관하게 한다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: Bags you give to the employee are called "checked bags," "checked baggage" or "checked luggage."
sentences.ko: 직원에게 맡기는 가방은 'checked bags', 'checked baggage', 'checked luggage'라고 해요.

sentences.en: Here’s the question airline employees ask to find out if you want to check bags:
sentences.ko: 짐을 부칠지 알아보려고 항공사 직원이 묻는 말은 이거예요.

sentences.en: Will you be checking any bags today?
Or, they may say it this way:
Do you have any checked bags today?
You can answer yes or no, and tell them how many:
sentences.ko: 있다 없다로 대답하고 몇 개인지 말하면 돼요.

sentences.en: Yes, just this one.
They will then tell you to put the bag on a machine to measure the weight.
sentences.ko: 그러면 무게를 재는 기계에 가방을 올려 달라고 할 거예요.

sentences.en: Here’s what they will say:
Please place your bag on the scale.
But some bags are small enough to fit in the passenger area of the plane.
sentences.ko: 그런데 어떤 가방은 작아서 비행기 객실에 들고 탈 수 있어요.

sentences.en: The bag you keep with you on the plane is called a “carry-on bag” or simply a “carry-on.”
sentences.ko: 비행기에 들고 타는 가방은 'carry-on bag', 줄여서 'carry-on'이라고 해요.

sentences.en: Sadly, there are times when your carry-on does not meet weight or size restrictions.
sentences.ko: 안타깝게도 기내 가방이 무게나 크기 제한을 넘을 때가 있어요.

sentences.en: In such cases, you’ll hear something like this: I’m sorry but your bag is too heavy.
sentences.ko: 그럴 때는 이런 말을 듣게 돼요. 죄송하지만 가방이 너무 무거워요.

sentences.en: You’ll have to check it.
I’m sorry.
Your bag is too big.
You’ll have to check it.
OK, so you’ve finished at the check-in area.
Now it’s time to go through security.
In line, you may hear a security employee announce this to the crowd:
sentences.ko: 줄을 서 있으면 보안 직원이 사람들에게 이렇게 안내할 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Please have your IDs and boarding passes out.
That means have your documents ready to show the security person.
sentences.ko: 보안 직원에게 보여 줄 서류를 준비하라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: Security workers also check bags and other belongings.
sentences.ko: 보안 직원은 가방과 다른 소지품도 검사해요.

sentences.en: Sometimes, you have to place such things in a plastic container called a “bin.”
sentences.ko: 가끔은 소지품을 '빈(bin)'이라는 플라스틱 바구니에 넣어야 해요.

sentences.en: Security workers may ask if you have any liquids, foods or medicines:
sentences.ko: 보안 직원이 액체나 음식, 약이 있는지 물을 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Are you traveling with any liquids?
OK, you made it through security with ease.
Congratulations!
Time to go to your gate – the seating area where you wait for your plane to board.
sentences.ko: 이제 탑승구로 갈 시간이에요. 비행기 탑승을 기다리며 앉아 있는 곳이죠.

sentences.en: At the gate, here’s an announcement you might hear:
sentences.ko: 탑승구에서는 이런 안내 방송을 들을 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Attention passengers on flight 95 to Chicago: Your flight has been delayed due to weather conditions.
sentences.ko: 시카고행 95편 승객 여러분께 알립니다. 기상 상황으로 비행기 출발이 늦어졌습니다.

sentences.en: The new departure time is 5:45.
So, your flight is delayed three hours.
sentences.ko: 그러니까 비행기가 세 시간 늦어진 거예요.

sentences.en: But, let’s say Chicago is not your final destination.
sentences.ko: 그런데 시카고가 최종 목적지가 아니라고 해 볼게요.

sentences.en: You are supposed to fly another plane from Chicago to your final destination.
sentences.ko: 시카고에서 다른 비행기를 타고 최종 목적지로 가야 하는 거죠.

sentences.en: That is called a “layover” in American English.
You might also hear it called a “stopover.”
The delay means you will miss your flight out of Chicago.
sentences.ko: 출발이 늦어지면 시카고에서 갈아탈 비행기를 놓치게 돼요.

sentences.en: But don’t worry!
Just let the person at the airline counter know:
sentences.ko: 항공사 카운터 직원에게 이렇게 말하면 돼요.

sentences.en: Hi, I missed my connecting flight to Los Angeles.
What should I do?
Airlines generally have solutions ready, such as putting you on the next flight or putting you in a hotel for the night.
sentences.ko: 항공사는 보통 다음 비행기에 태워 주거나 그날 밤 호텔을 잡아 주는 식으로 해결책을 마련해 두고 있어요.

sentences.en: After an international flight, you will be directed through customs.
sentences.ko: 국제선을 타고 내리면 세관 쪽으로 안내받게 돼요.

sentences.en: That is where government officers approve or reject entrance into the country.
sentences.ko: 정부 직원이 입국을 허가하거나 거절하는 곳이에요.

sentences.en: The customs officer will ask for your passport and may or may not have questions.
sentences.ko: 세관 직원이 여권을 달라고 하고, 질문을 할 수도 있고 안 할 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: Here are five common questions you might hear at customs:
sentences.ko: 세관에서 자주 듣는 질문 다섯 가지를 알려 드릴게요.

sentences.en: What is the purpose of your trip?
How long do you intend to stay?
Can I see your return ticket?
Where will you be staying?
What is your occupation?
Preparing this information before your trip will help make the process easier.
sentences.ko: 여행 전에 이런 정보를 준비해 두면 절차가 더 쉬워져요.

sentences.en: For example, if you’re staying with a friend or at a hotel, have the person or hotel’s name and address ready.
sentences.ko: 예를 들어 친구 집이나 호텔에 묵는다면 그 사람이나 호텔의 이름과 주소를 준비해 두세요.

sentences.en: I’m Alice Bryant.

contents.title: What 'Strikes a Chord' with You?
contents.title_ko: 마음을 울리는 것: strike a chord

sentences.en: And now, Words and Their Stories, from VOA Learning English.
On this program, we explore words and expressions in the English language.
sentences.ko: 이 프로그램에서는 영어 낱말과 표현을 살펴봐요.

sentences.en: We give examples that show how to use them.
sentences.ko: 어떻게 쓰는지 보여 주는 예도 들고요.

sentences.en: And sometimes we explain where they come from.
Today, our expression comes from music.
A chord is three or more musical notes sounded at the same time.
sentences.ko: 코드(chord)는 세 개 이상의 음을 동시에 내는 화음이에요.

sentences.en: The word “strike” means to hit.
But when we play a note on a musical instrument, we can also say we struck a note.
sentences.ko: 그런데 악기로 음 하나를 연주할 때도 음을 'strike'했다고 말할 수 있어요.

sentences.en: So, our expression for today is to strike a chord.
In its most general definition, to strike a chord means something relates to you somehow.
sentences.ko: 가장 넓은 뜻으로 'strike a chord'는 무언가가 어떤 식으로든 나와 연결된다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: It resonates with you.
If something strikes a chord with you, it is familiar to you in some way, for better or for worse.
sentences.ko: 무언가가 'strike a chord with you' 한다면, 좋든 나쁘든 어떤 면에서 익숙하게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: Something can strike a positive chord.
sentences.ko: 어떤 것은 좋은 쪽으로 마음을 울릴 수 있어요.

sentences.en: It is familiar to you in a good way.
It creates good feelings or thoughts.
For example, a love song struck a deep chord with James.
sentences.ko: 예를 들어, 어떤 사랑 노래가 제임스의 마음을 깊이 울렸어요.

sentences.en: It is the song he sang to his wife at their wedding.
sentences.ko: 결혼식 날 아내에게 불러 준 노래거든요.

sentences.en: Or maybe the song was playing on the radio when she left him.
sentences.ko: 아니면 아내가 그를 떠날 때 라디오에서 그 노래가 나오고 있었을지도 모르죠.

sentences.en: In that case, the song would strike a negative chord with James.
sentences.ko: 그렇다면 그 노래는 제임스의 마음을 아프게 울릴 거예요.

sentences.en: As you can see from those examples, you can add other words to describe what type of chord is being struck – a deep chord, a negative chord.
sentences.ko: 이 예에서 보듯이 다른 낱말을 더해서 어떤 울림인지 나타낼 수 있어요. 깊은 울림, 부정적인 울림처럼요.

sentences.en: Here are some other examples.
A teacher’s advice can strike a responsive chord with students.
sentences.ko: 선생님의 조언이 학생들의 마음에 와닿을 수 있어요.

sentences.en: And a politician’s speech can strike a sympathetic chord with voters.
sentences.ko: 정치인의 연설이 유권자들의 공감을 살 수도 있고요.

sentences.en: Those two words – sympathetic and responsive – are commonly used with this expression.
sentences.ko: sympathetic(공감하는)과 responsive(호응하는), 이 두 낱말은 이 표현과 자주 함께 써요.

sentences.en: You might hear people say something “struck a familiar chord.”
sentences.ko: 사람들이 무언가가 'struck a familiar chord'라고 말하는 걸 들을 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: But to me, this sounds a bit unnecessary.
sentences.ko: 그런데 제 귀에는 좀 불필요하게 들려요.

sentences.en: If something strikes a chord, it means it is familiar in some way.
sentences.ko: 'strike a chord' 자체가 어떤 면에서 익숙하다는 뜻이니까요.

sentences.en: So, we don’t need to add the word “familiar” to the expression.
sentences.ko: 그래서 이 표현에 'familiar'를 덧붙일 필요가 없어요.

sentences.en: But I have heard it used that way before.
sentences.ko: 그래도 그렇게 쓰는 걸 들어 본 적은 있어요.

sentences.en: Maybe it means something is really familiar.
Sometimes we use to strike a chord this way: If something creates strong feelings or thoughts, it strikes a chord.
sentences.ko: 가끔은 이렇게도 써요. 무언가가 강한 감정이나 생각을 불러일으키면 'strike a chord' 한다고요.

sentences.en: And that “something” could be unfamiliar to the person.
sentences.ko: 그 '무언가'는 그 사람에게 낯선 것일 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: Here is another situation where we use this expression: If something strikes a chord with you, you approve of it.
sentences.ko: 이 표현을 쓰는 상황이 하나 더 있어요. 무언가가 'strike a chord with you' 한다면 그걸 좋게 본다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: You agree with it.
For example, during the election the politician’s position on the economy and jobs must have struck a chord with voters because she won easily.
sentences.ko: 예를 들어 선거 때 그 정치인이 경제와 일자리에 대해 낸 생각이 유권자들의 마음을 움직였나 봐요. 쉽게 당선됐거든요.

sentences.en: Let’s talk for a minute about sentence structure.
sentences.ko: 잠깐 문장 구조 이야기를 해 볼게요.

sentences.en: If you look back at our examples, most if not all of them use the word “with" – with James, with students, with voters.
sentences.ko: 앞의 예를 다시 보면 거의 다 'with'를 써요. with James, with students, with voters처럼요.

sentences.en: But you can use this expression without the word “with.”
sentences.ko: 하지만 'with' 없이도 이 표현을 쓸 수 있어요.

sentences.en: In this way, “strike a chord” means it caused a strong emotional reaction to something.
sentences.ko: 이렇게 쓰면 'strike a chord'는 무언가에 강한 감정 반응을 일으켰다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: For example, that movie must have really struck a chord.
sentences.ko: 예를 들어 그 영화는 정말 사람들의 마음을 울렸나 봐요.

sentences.en: Everyone came out of the theater crying.
Hopefully learning English continues to strike a chord with all of you … a positive one!
sentences.ko: 영어 공부도 여러분 모두의 마음을 계속 울리길 바라요... 좋은 쪽으로요!

sentences.en: And that’s the end of this Words and Their Stories.
Until next time … I’m Anna Matteo.
